candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Information Technology, printed p.22 / PDF p.26: enter computer documentation accurately, completely and in a timely manner
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Information Technology / telehealth documentation
candidate.educational_objective: Document telehealth encounters as clinical encounters in the health record and identify the telehealth modality of care without reducing documentation completeness.

options.A: Document the clinical encounter in the health record and identify that the encounter was conducted by telehealth
options.B: Document only the billing code because clinical notes are unnecessary for a virtual encounter
options.C: Omit the encounter from the health record unless the client specifically asks for documentation
options.D: Use less complete clinical documentation than would be required for comparable in-person care

candidate.rationale: HHS telehealth workflow guidance directs clinicians to document that an encounter was a telehealth visit, and federal documentation guidance continues to require complete clinical documentation of patient encounters. Therefore A is correct. A virtual modality does not remove the need for a clinical record, and documentation is not optional based on patient request.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A telehealth encounter should be documented in the clinical record and identified as a telehealth visit; telehealth does not eliminate clinical documentation requirements.
candidate.source_locator: Follow up after telehealth visits — Documentation: document that this was a telehealth visit; use telehealth-specific billing codes/modifiers as applicable; workflow includes documentation as a core process
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — Telehealth.HHS.gov
candidate.stem: After completing a telehealth encounter, which documentation practice is appropriate?
